name: Kedarkantha
summary: India's most popular winter summit trek through snow-laden pine forests to a 360° Himalayan view.
description: Starting from the village of Sankri in Govind Wildlife Sanctuary, the Kedarkantha trail climbs through dense pine and oak forests to the frozen Juda ka Talab and a series of snowy campsites. The summit push begins before dawn and rewards trekkers with views of Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch and Black Peak.
permits: Forest entry permit for Govind Wildlife Sanctuary (arranged at Sankri)

name: Hampta Pass
summary: A dramatic crossover from the green Kullu valley to the stark desert of Lahaul, with a side trip to Chandratal.
description: Hampta Pass connects the lush meadows of Kullu with the barren landscapes of Lahaul–Spiti. The trail follows river crossings, flower-filled meadows at Chika and Balu ka Ghera before the pass, and descends to Shea Goru. Most batches end with a drive to Chandratal lake.
highlights: Valley crossover from green to desert
permits: Forest permit from Manali forest office

name: Rajmachi Fort
summary: A classic Sahyadri fort trek with twin citadels, waterfalls and fireflies in the pre-monsoon nights.
description: Rajmachi has two fortifications, Shrivardhan and Manaranjan, overlooking the Konkan and Ulhas valley. The wide jeep trail from Lonavala is gentle, making it ideal for first-timers, while the steeper Kondivade route from Karjat offers a tougher climb.
